Sufganiyot

Served at: Hanukkah (Festival of Lights)

Makes about 12 doughnutsPrep 2 hours 30 minutesCook 20 minutes

Sufganiyot are traditional Jewish jelly-filled doughnuts enjoyed during Hanukkah, the Festival of Lights. They symbolize the miracle of the oil that lasted eight days, as they are fried in oil to commemorate this event.

Ingredients

  • 2 1/4 teaspoons active dry yeast (1 packet)
  • 1/4 cup warm water (110°F/43°C)
  • 1/2 cup warm milk (110°F/43°C)
  • 1/4 cup granulated sugar
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/4 cup unsalted butter, melted
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 3 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • Vegetable oil for frying
  • 1 cup strawberry or raspberry jam
  • Powdered sugar for dusting

Method

  1. In a small bowl, dissolve yeast in warm water and let sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine warm milk, sugar, eggs, melted butter, and vanilla extract.
  3. Add the yeast mixture to the wet ingredients and stir to combine.
  4. Gradually add flour and salt, mixing until a soft dough forms.
  5. Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  6. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a clean towel, and let rise in a warm place for about 1 to 1 1/2 hours, or until doubled in size.
  7. Punch down the dough and roll it out to about 1/4 inch (0.6 cm) thickness.
  8. Use a round cutter (about 3 inches/7.5 cm diameter) to cut out circles of dough.
  9. Place the dough circles on a floured baking sheet, cover, and let rise for another 30 minutes.
  10. Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
  11. Fry the doughnuts in batches for about 1-2 minutes per side, until golden brown.
  12. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
  13. Once cooled slightly, use a piping bag or a small spoon to fill each doughnut with jam.
  14. Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.

Tips

  • Make sure the oil temperature is steady to avoid greasy or undercooked doughnuts.
  • You can substitute the jam with chocolate or custard filling for variety.
  • For a lighter doughnut, let the dough rise longer to develop more airiness.
